event_description: J. Watumull Planetarium Sunday, September 13, 2026 Sunday, September 27, 2026 Sunday, October 4, 2026 Sunday, October 11, 2026 Sunday, November 22, 2026 Sunday, December 6, 2026 Sunday, December 27, 2026 Two Showtimes Available 5:30-6:30 p.m. and 7:00-8:00 p.m. Advance Online Registration Required General Admission: $5 per person; lap children (ages 0-2) are free Members: Free, but must reserve tickets in advance   Not a member? Join today! Program Overview Now playing: the extended cut of a planetarium show favorite, T. REX! Chronicling the true story of three boys’ discovery of a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex fossil in July 2022 in North Dakota, T. REX takes you through the life and times of this iconic dinosaur. Transport yourself back in time to explore prehistoric Earth with Cretaceous creatures through this blend of documentary and CGI artistry. Produced by Giant Screen Films. Narrated by Jurassic Park actor Sam Neill. Admission includes access only to the J. Watumull Planetarium lobby exhibit, Wayfinders: He Waʻa He Moku, He Moku He Waʻa and a seat for one screening of T. REX in the planetarium theater. Evening’s Schedule 5:00 p.m. - Check-in begins in the Planetarium lobby 5:15 p.m. - Seating begins for for 5:30 p.m. ticketholders 5:30 p.m. - Show begins with a live-presented exploration of the night sky. Then, sit back and enjoy T. REX (42 min)! One-hour-long seated theater experience. 6:30 p.m. - Film concludes; lobby exhibit open for exploration; Check-in continues in lobby. 6:45 p.m. - Seating begins for 7:00 p.m. ticketholders 7:00 p.m. - Show begins with a live-presented exploration of the night sky. Then, sit back and enjoy T. REX (42 min)! One-hour-long seated theater experience. 8:00 p.m. - Film concludes; lobby exhibit open for exploration 8:30 p.m. - Closure of lobby and end of event   Additional Details This is an in-person event at the J. Watumull Planetarium at Bishop Museum. No online options or recordings will be available. Seating is first come, first served. No late seating. Doors close at 5:30 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. when each program begins. Please plan to arrive no later than 10 minutes prior to selected showtime. Check-in and entry will be near Bishop Museum’s Shop Pacifica (front entrance and gift shop). The check-in area will be located at the top of the main staircase/ramp and to the right. Check-in for selected showtime begins as early as 30 minutes prior to show start. Doors open for seating 15 minutes prior to show start and the theater is open seating. No food or drink will be sold at the planetarium. There is no eating or drinking inside the theater. The planetarium is fairly cool; you may want to bring a light sweater. Please pay for parking using a mobile phone through a posted Parklinq QR code (card payments only) or have your member parking sticker on your car. Please see Directions and Parking for more information. Parking in Museum lots is $5.00/vehicle after 5:00 p.m. Tickets are fully refundable until two hours before the selected showtime. Refunds can be issued over the phone at (808) 847-3511 or via email at visitorexperience@bishopmuseum.org. Less than two hours before the scheduled start of the first show, ticket sales are non-refundable. Refunds not available for no-shows or late arrivals. For additional information about evening planetarium programs, please call (808) 848-4108 or email planetarium@bishopmuseum.org.

event_name: Museum After Hours
event_description: Once a month, Bishop Museum opens its 15‑acre campus after sunset, inviting kamaʻāina and visitors to explore Hawaiʻi’s rich cultural and natural heritage in a vibrant evening setting. During Bishop Museum After Hours, guests can wander through Hawaiian Hall to experience treasures such as Kalaniʻōpuʻu’s ʻahu ʻula (feather cloak) and mahiole (helmet); dive into Hawaiʻi’s extraordinary biodiversity in the Science Adventure Center; and enjoy our newest exhibitions in the Castle Memorial Building and J. M. Long Gallery. This enhanced After Hours experience now proudly incorporates the former Kaiwiʻula Night Market, expanding our on‑campus marketplace with an even greater selection of local food, drink, and dessert vendors, along with a curated lineup of local artisans and craft makers. It’s the perfect opportunity to support Hawaiʻi businesses while enjoying the museum under Honolulu’s star‑lit sky. Relax on the Great Lawn with ʻono eats, browse unique handcrafted goods, and enjoy live Hawaiian music throughout the evening. With a special reduced evening admission rate for kamaʻāina, Bishop Museum After Hours offers expanded access to the Museum’s collections, stories, and research — making it easier than ever for the community to connect with Hawaiʻi’s natural and cultural heritage.

event_name: Shells, Wings %26 Wonder
event_description: An Architectural LEGO® Workshop Saturday, October 10, 2026 Gallery Lawns 10:00 a.m. - 2:00 p.m. FREE with Museum Admission Celebrate the closing weekend of Aloha Bricks ’26: Stories of Hawaiʻi with American Institute of Architects, Hawaiʻi chapter (AIA Hawaiʻi)! AIA Hawaiʻi invites you to a hands-on architectural workshop celebrating the Museum’s newest exhibit, Aloha Bricks LEGO®. Led by local architects, this interactive session draws from the Museum’s collections to explore how nature informs the built environment. Perfect for keiki and the young at heart, this workshop invites participants to see architecture through the lens of Hawaiʻi’s unique biodiversity—where shells become homes, wings become structures, and imagination builds the rest. Workshops will be offered in 30-minute intervals allowing guests to drop in, build, and explore at their own pace.

event_name: The Stars Tonight
event_description: Bishop Museum’s J. Watumull Planetarium Presents The Stars Tonight 7:00–8:00 p.m. HST In-person at the J. Watumull Planetarium All ages welcome Online Registration Required* General Admission: $10 per adult, $7 per youth 4-17, 3 and under free** Members: 50% off general admission member tickets Not a member? Join today! Evening’s Schedule Join us for the Stars Tonight at Bishop Museum! Examine the skies with a presenter in our planetarium, featuring the stars, planets, astronomical highlights, and other stories of the current season. 6:30 p.m. – Check-in begins. Enjoy planetarium lobby exhibits and views over the Great Lawn. 6:45 p.m. - Show seating begins. 7:00 p.m. – The Stars Tonight planetarium show presentation. All ages welcome. One-hour-long seated theater experience. 8:00 p.m. - Stargazing, weather permitting, with the Hawaiian Astronomical Society. 9:00 p.m. - Event close.   *Tickets are only available for purchase online. No on-site registration will be allowed at the event. No entry without confirmed pre-registration due to limited seating. **Guests 3 and under will be expected to share a seat with an adult/guardian. Program Details: This is an in-person event at the J. Watumull Planetarium at Bishop Museum. No online options or recordings will be available. Seating is first come, first served. No late seating. Doors close at 7:00 p.m. when the program begins. Please plan to arrive no later than 6:45 p.m. Check-in and entry will be near Bishop Museum’s Shop Pacifica (front entrance and gift shop). The check-in table will be located at the top of the main staircase/ramp and to the right. Check-in and viewing of the planetarium lobby will begin at 6:30 p.m. Doors open for planetarium seating at 6:45 p.m. The presentation will begin at 7:00 p.m. and last approximately an hour. No food or drink allowed in the planetarium. The planetarium is fairly cool, you may want to bring a light sweater. Evening parking is $5. Please pay for parking using a mobile phone through a posted Parking QR code (card payments only) or have your member parking sticker on your car. Please see Directions and Parking for more information. Tickets are fully refundable until 6:00 p.m. the night of the show. Refunds can be issued over the phone at (808) 847-3511 or via email at visitorexperience@bishopmuseum.org. After 6:00 p.m., less than 1 hour before the scheduled start of the show, ticket sales are non-refundable. Refunds not available for no-shows or late arrivals. For additional information about evening planetarium programs, please call (808) 847-3511 or email visitorexperience@bishopmuseum.org both are monitored during Museum business hours of 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

event_name: Behind the Scenes Native Garden Tour
event_description: Saturday, October 24 from 10:00 AM - 12:00 PM Location: Bishop Museum Native Garden Free with museum admission, registration required Join expert botanist, Miles Thomas, on an in-depth native garden tour! Take a guided walk through the garden and learn how to identify native and canoe plant species. We’ll also discuss the cultural and historical significance of some of the flora we have on Bishop Museum campus. This event will be outdoors with limited shade access, so please plan accordingly: Bring water, sunscreen and an enthusiasm for plants! After the walk, participants will be gifted a native Hawaiian plant to take home and can spend some time talking story and try Hawaiian grown ʻawa. This event will be outside with minimal shade, so please bring water, sun protection, and dress accordingly. This workshop is part of Bishop Museum’s ʻāina based community experiences, to educate and connect the public with our ʻāina in the museum’s open air learning spaces.

event_name: Nānā I Ke Kumu: He Hoʻoilina Ola Ka Hula
event_description: The Living Hula Legacy of Mary Kawena Pukui Through Archival Film, Audio, Photographs, and Hula (1930–1945) November 7, 2026 | 5:30 p.m.–8 p.m. Hawaiian Hall | Gallery Lawns $25 General Admission, $10 for Ages 17 and Under Free for Museum Members In partnership with the Mary Kawena Pukui Cultural Preservation Society, Bishop Museum invites you to celebrate the life, work, and enduring legacy of Mary Kawena Pukui, a foundational pillar of Hawaiian knowledge and cultural revitalization. Nānā i ke Kumu 2026: He Hoʻoilina Ola Ka Hula celebrates traditional hula carried through the Pukui hula lineage: a living legacy of movement, mele, language, lore, and ʻike passed from generation to generation. Inspired by the hula and mele presentations Mrs. Pukui organized in Hawaiian Hall during her tenure at Bishop Museum and throughout Hawaiʻi paeʻāina, the program draws upon research by Pelehonuamea Harman and Kimo Alama Keaulana and Pukui’s own program notes to bring forward traditional hula and mele that are rarely seen or practiced today. The evening will feature the premiere of newly restored archival footage from the 1930s and 1940s, including hula foot movements demonstrated by Patience Nāmaka Bacon and traditional hand gestures. Archival film, audio, photographs, narration, mele, and live hula will come together to illuminate this ʻike as more than a record of the past, but rather, as a living hula legacy that endures today. Join us for this special evening honoring Mrs. Pukui’s contributions to ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi, moʻolelo, hula, mele, and the perpetuation of ʻike kupuna.
